title: Archer weaves
summary: Keep one hand extended and the other beside the opposite shoulder, then thread a staff on each side of that shoulder. Drex teaches this weave in split-time opposites.

setup.grip: Hold each staff at its center; identify the thumb and pinky ends. Begin with both thumb ends up.
setup.stance: Begin facing forward with room to turn slightly. Extend the right arm and bring the left hand near the right shoulder.
setup.plane: The staves travel around the shoulder and upper arm, with front and behind positions. The path is not one flat wall-plane circle.

moves.name: Shoulder-hand drill
moves.description: Learn the close-hand path before adding the extended-hand staff.
moves.grip: Left hand holds the center with thumb end initially up.
moves.stance: Right arm reaches sideways; left hand stays near the right shoulder.
moves.focus: Alternate which end passes behind the shoulder, with clearance for the extended arm.

steps.title: Thumb end behind
steps.body: Keep the right arm extended. Lower the left staff's thumb end behind the right shoulder so its pinky end rises.

steps.title: Return over the shoulder
steps.body: Aim the pinky end outward to your right, lower it, and recover the thumb end upward. Keep the staff controlled in your hand; the shoulder is a spatial cue.

steps.title: Pass under the arm
steps.body: Aim the thumb end outward beneath the right arm. Lift the pinky end behind the arm, then turn it outward to return to thumb-up.

steps.title: Join the two passages
steps.body: Repeat slowly: the staff gets a passage in front of the shoulder and a passage behind it. Let the extended arm make room.

diagramNotes: Show front/behind shoulder occlusion or a side view. A flat tip-circle alone cannot explain the arm threading.

moves.name: Two-staff archer weave
moves.description: Add the extended staff while preserving the shoulder weave.
moves.grip: Both staffs remain center-gripped. Start with thumb ends up.
moves.stance: Right hand extended; left hand beside right shoulder.
moves.focus: Use the two inward-facing checkpoints and keep room between the staves.

steps.title: Thumb ends face inward
steps.body: Turn the left thumb end toward your right and the right thumb end toward your left. The thumb ends now aim toward one another.

steps.title: Pinky ends rise
steps.body: Move the extended right hand slightly back for clearance while both pinky ends rise. Bring the pinky ends inward, then return both thumb ends upward.

steps.title: Thread the next passage
steps.body: Repeat the inward checkpoint. This time one rising pinky end is behind the right shoulder and the other is in front. Recover through pinky-ends-in to thumb-ends-up.

steps.title: Smooth the path
steps.body: Connect the stops gradually. Drex describes a V-shaped travel around the body while the staves remain nearly parallel and the arm supplies separation.

moves.timing: Split-time opposites, as named in the tutorial
diagramNotes: Requires the shoulder, upper arm and front/behind passages. Do not infer timing solely from the two visible tip colors.

moves.name: Other side and side-to-side weave
moves.description: Repeat on the other shoulder, then explore transferring between sides.
moves.grip: Keep the same center grips and thumb/pinky labels.
moves.stance: Mirror the extended and shoulder hands on the left side.
moves.focus: Make the mirrored shoulder passage comfortable before linking sides.

steps.title: Mirror the setup
steps.body: Extend the left arm and bring the right hand toward the left shoulder. Rebuild the solo path and then add the second staff.

steps.title: Link sides
steps.body: Once both sides are smooth, explore traveling between them as demonstrated at the end. Keep the shoulder clearance visible and move slowly.

diagramNotes: This is a brief demonstration, not a detailed transfer breakdown. The diagram may show the two endpoint setups; use the source for the continuous transfer.

pitfalls: Keeping the extended arm rigidly in the staff's path. Make small clearance adjustments.
Flattening the shoulder weave into a single plane; one passage must be in front and another behind.
Speeding up before both inward-facing checkpoints are repeatable.
Treating the shoulder cue as a release or contact balance; the staff remains held.

evidence.observation: Drex explicitly calls the demonstrated weave split-time opposites and contrasts it with the poi version.
Direct frame shows left hand near the right shoulder, right arm extended and left thumb end up.
Direct frame and surrounding narration show the pinky end rising behind the extended arm.
Direct frame shows the two thumb ends pointing inward before the paired shoulder passage.
Direct frame falls in the passage where the two rising pinky ends occupy front/behind positions relative to the shoulder.
Drex describes the V-shaped travel and nearly parallel staves.
The ending asks learners to learn the other side and transfer between sides.

limitations: This analysis uses the downloaded video, its captions and direct timestamped frames; diagrams are teaching schematics rather than motion capture.
Drex is tentative about weave beat counting here, so no numerical beat count is assigned.
The mirrored-side transfer is only briefly shown.
The spoken paired sequence includes a correction around 5:07; use the demonstrated front/behind cycle instead of treating that false start as a separate variant.

title: Basic transitions
summary: Connect timing and direction combinations at shared positions, then change driving style and prop facing. Finish by using those connections to enter choo-choos.

setup.grip: Use the center grips from the foundational lessons. Keep track of which end lies on the thumb side of each hand.
setup.stance: Stand comfortably with room for full arm circles and occasional torso turns.
setup.plane: Begin in the familiar wall-plane patterns. Learn shared hand positions before adding travel or plane changes.

moves.name: Shared positions and the isolation cycle
moves.description: Find the four cardinal hand positions that let one timing/direction combination become another.
moves.grip: Maintain your center grips; first follow hand positions rather than changing grip.
moves.stance: Face the pattern with room above, below and on both sides.
moves.focus: Change at a shared position instead of adding an extra loop.

steps.title: Locate the four points
steps.body: With together-same isolations, identify bottom, left, top and right. Side positions also belong to split opposites; top and bottom also belong to together opposites.

steps.title: Change one relationship
steps.body: At a common point, reverse the appropriate hand's travel while the other continues. Check the next timing/direction before completing the next circle.

steps.title: Walk the cycle
steps.body: Practice together same, together opposites, split same, split opposites, then together same. Pause at each shared position until the route is clear.

moves.timing: Together same → together opposites → split same → split opposites → together same

moves.name: Antispin timing cycle
moves.description: Apply the same shared-position route while both hands drive antispins.
moves.grip: Center grips; preserve the current thumb/pinky facing while learning the timing route.
moves.stance: Stay in wall plane with space for the antispin corners.
moves.focus: Find a common checkpoint in the antispin pattern before changing direction.

steps.title: Establish together same
steps.body: Make the antispin pattern stable with both hands following together.

steps.title: Cycle the four modes
steps.body: At shared positions, progress to together opposites, split same, split opposites and back to together same.

steps.title: Check the corners
steps.body: Pause if necessary at each transition. Resume the antispin geometry once the new hand relationship is established.

moves.timing: Together same → together opposites → split same → split opposites → together same

moves.name: Antispin to isolation and back
moves.description: Change the driving style at a position that both shapes share.
moves.grip: Retain the grips and notice whether the thumb or pinky ends face inward after the change.
moves.stance: Start with the antispin checkpoint above the body.
moves.focus: Match position first, then choose a different route away from it.

steps.title: Meet at the top
steps.body: Bring the two antispin paths to the top checkpoint used in the demonstration.

steps.title: Choose isolation
steps.body: From that shared position, continue with together-opposite isolations instead of another antispin section.

steps.title: Return through the checkpoint
steps.body: Use a compatible shared position to resume antispins. Watch both the hand route and the end facing.

moves.timing: Together opposites at the demonstrated switch

moves.name: Alternate driving styles around the cycle
moves.description: Combine the four timing modes with alternating antispin and isolation.
moves.grip: Center grips remain fixed; inspect the prop facing at each handover.
moves.stance: Use full, comfortable arm circles in front of the body.
moves.focus: Change timing and driving style deliberately at the shared checkpoints.

steps.title: Start with antispin
steps.body: Begin together-same antispins and move into together-opposite isolations.

steps.title: Alternate again
steps.body: Continue into split-same antispins, then split-opposite isolations.

steps.title: Close the cycle
steps.body: Return to together-same antispins. Note that the resulting inward-facing ends may differ from the starting setup.

moves.timing: Together-same antispin → together-opposite isolation → split-same antispin → split-opposite isolation

moves.name: Prop-facing changes with hybrids
moves.description: Use a short hybrid segment plus a matched driving segment to change which ends face inward.
moves.grip: Track the thumb-side end explicitly; the hand does not need to swap its grip on the staff.
moves.stance: Work at clear vertical and side checkpoints in front of the body.
moves.focus: A change in facing is separate from a change in timing/direction.

steps.title: Observe the hybrid
steps.body: An isolation/antispin hybrid can take matching thumb-end facings into a position with one thumb end up and the other down.

steps.title: Use the quarter-beat bridge
steps.body: As demonstrated, combine a quarter-beat hybrid segment with a quarter-beat segment where both props use the same driving style. One example uses antispin for the matched segment.

steps.title: Reverse the facing change
steps.body: Try the shown isolation quarter-beat followed by a hybrid quarter-beat. Stop at the endpoint and check which end of each staff points inward.

moves.timing: Short hybrid and homogeneous segments; inspect the resulting facing
diagramNotes: The tutorial also illustrates a half isolation circuit before returning to the hybrid at 6:01. Quarter-beat is Drex's term for the short demonstrated segments, not a universal duration in seconds.

moves.name: Isolation to choo-choos and back
moves.description: Use a hybrid bridge to connect split-same isolations with the choo-choo setup.
moves.grip: Center grips; prepare the prop facings shown at the bridge endpoint.
moves.stance: Allow the torso to turn slightly as the two paths come into line.
moves.focus: Finish the bridge in the correct facing before starting choo-choos.

steps.title: Start with isolations
steps.body: Establish split-time same-direction isolations.

steps.title: Bridge to the target
steps.body: Use the shown hybrid, arrive in split-opposite antispin, then continue into choo-choos.

steps.title: Open back out
steps.body: Hybrid back, isolate open, and resume split-same isolations. Together-opposite isolation is another shown continuation.

moves.timing: Split-same isolation → hybrid → split-opposite antispin → choo-choo

moves.name: Repeat the cycle with inspin
moves.description: The closing exercise extends the same four-mode cycle to inspins.
moves.grip: Keep a center grip and use the inspin-facing setup learned earlier.
moves.stance: Keep enough room for the larger arm-driven circles.
moves.focus: Practice one driving style at a time before mixing them.

steps.title: Repeat the four checkpoints
steps.body: Work through the timing/direction cycle with isolations, then antispins, then inspins.

steps.title: Keep the style consistent
steps.body: During the inspin round, keep the staff rotation working with the arm circle as you change timing mode.

moves.timing: Cycle through all four timing/direction combinations

moves.name: Combined transition drill
moves.description: Put the lesson together by alternating driving styles and then adding prop-facing changes.
moves.grip: Keep the same grip; pause to verify thumb/pinky orientation when the facing changes.
moves.stance: Stay in a comfortable wall-plane working area.
moves.focus: Add one transition layer at a time.

steps.title: Mix the driving styles
steps.body: Alternate antispin and isolation at shared positions while moving through the timing cycle.

steps.title: Add facing changes
steps.body: Once the route is steady, insert the short hybrid bridges that change the inward-facing ends.

steps.title: Recover deliberately
steps.body: If a transition reaches an unintended pattern, stop at a known checkpoint and restart. The demonstration itself includes corrections.

pitfalls: Switching between shapes without checking that the hand and staff positions actually match.
Treating timing/direction and prop facing as the same variable.
Losing track of the thumb-side end after a hybrid.
Trying the full mixed drill before the individual isolation, antispin and inspin cycles are comfortable.

evidence.observation: The lesson explicitly separates timing/direction from prop facing.
Together-same side checkpoints are identified as shared with split opposites.
Together-same top and bottom checkpoints are identified as shared with together opposites.
The isolation cycle proceeds through all four timing/direction combinations.
Drex switches antispins to together-opposite isolations at the top.
He states the hybrid-plus-homogeneous quarter-beat rule for changing facing.
Direct frame shows the horizontal checkpoint during the isolation-plus-hybrid facing example.
Direct frame shows the vertical stack before the demonstrated choo-choo continuation.
The closing exercise explicitly includes inspins.

limitations: The opening 0:12-0:43 is an abandoned introduction; teaching begins with the restarted introduction at 0:47.
Several live demonstrations contain spoken self-corrections. The lesson follows the stated corrected sequence.
The short hybrid bridges are demonstrated more clearly than they are verbally enumerated. Use the linked source for exact end orientation before reproducing a bridge.
These are source-grounded practice summaries, not motion-captured trajectories.

title: Basic 3D
summary: Add toward and away points to the usual up, down, left and right diamond. Practice changing planes in each timing/direction combination.

setup.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
setup.stance: Begin facing the audience with space in front, behind and above; allow comfortable torso turns.
setup.plane: The six reference points form an octahedron around the body: up, down, left, right, toward the audience and away. Begin in wall plane and deliberately travel through depth.

moves.name: One-staff six-point exploration
moves.description: Add front and back reference points to the four wall-plane antispin points.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Begin facing the audience with space in front, behind and above; allow comfortable torso turns.
moves.focus: Make the plane change at a clear cardinal checkpoint.

steps.title: Map the diamond
steps.body: With one staff, find right, top, left and bottom in an antispin. Add a point toward the audience and a point away from them.

steps.title: Explore the side exit
steps.body: At a side checkpoint, carry the pinky end toward the audience and recover toward the body before continuing the wall-plane antispin.

steps.title: Explore the bottom exit
steps.body: At the bottom checkpoint, send the thumb end toward the audience and recover into the antispin. Keep the center grip while changing the plane.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

moves.name: Together-same side shifts
moves.description: Move both antispins through the audience-facing point at a side checkpoint.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Begin facing the audience with space in front, behind and above; allow comfortable torso turns.
moves.focus: Let both staves change plane together.

steps.title: Reach the right side
steps.body: Start together-same antispins. Pause at the right-side position with both hands following the same route.

steps.title: Travel through depth
steps.body: Send both pinky ends toward the audience, then recover the thumb ends toward the left-side position and continue the antispin.

steps.title: Repeat from the left
steps.body: At the left-side checkpoint, use the corresponding outward passage and return to the wall-plane route.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

moves.name: Together-same top and bottom shifts
moves.description: Take the same paired plane change between the low and high checkpoints.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Begin facing the audience with space in front, behind and above; allow comfortable torso turns.
moves.focus: Use the demonstrated thumb-end facing for this setup.

steps.title: Leave the bottom
steps.body: From both staves down, direct the thumb ends toward the audience and recover up into the next part of the pattern.

steps.title: Leave the top
steps.body: From the top checkpoint, pass the thumb ends toward the audience and recover toward the bottom before continuing around.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

moves.name: Together-same alternating plane-shift drill
moves.description: First repeat side shifts, then top/bottom shifts, then alternate all four exits.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Begin facing the audience with space in front, behind and above; allow comfortable torso turns.
moves.focus: Visit three points around the wall-plane diamond before each crossing.

steps.title: Separate the axes
steps.body: Repeat right-to-left/left-to-right shifts. Then repeat top-to-bottom/bottom-to-top shifts.

steps.title: Alternate the exits
steps.body: Cross right to left, later top to bottom, later left to right, then bottom to top.

steps.title: Count the wall-plane travel
steps.body: After a plane shift lands on the opposite point, visit the next three diamond points before shifting again.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

moves.name: Together-same isolation variation
moves.description: Repeat the same depth exits with isolations instead of antispins.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Begin facing the audience with space in front, behind and above; allow comfortable torso turns.
moves.focus: Change the driving style while retaining the six-point spatial map.

steps.title: Establish isolation
steps.body: Set the two isolations together and locate the same side and vertical checkpoints.

steps.title: Drag through depth
steps.body: Use the demonstrated isolation path to carry the staves across to the opposite point, then return to the wall-plane isolation.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

moves.name: Together-opposite side shifts
moves.description: Use the front point to move between open and crossed-arm positions.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Begin facing the audience; allow the arms to cross comfortably in front.
moves.focus: Open and crossed positions are both valid entrances.

steps.title: Start open
steps.body: With pinky ends out to the sides, direct the thumb ends toward the audience.

steps.title: Cross through the passage
steps.body: Carry the arms into the crossed position as the pinky ends travel away from the body, then continue the antispins.

steps.title: Start crossed
steps.body: Repeat from crossed arms, send the thumb ends toward the audience, and return through to the open position.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

moves.name: Together-opposite vertical shifts
moves.description: Take both staves from top to bottom, or bottom to top, through the front point.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Begin facing the audience with space in front, behind and above; allow comfortable torso turns.
moves.focus: This demonstrated facing uses pinky ends toward the audience.

steps.title: Top exit
steps.body: At the upper checkpoint, aim the pinky ends toward the audience and recover through the lower position.

steps.title: Bottom exit
steps.body: At the lower checkpoint, pass the pinky ends toward the audience and continue up.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

moves.name: Together-opposite alternating drill
moves.description: Combine open, top, crossed and bottom exits into one practice cycle.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Keep the body comfortable as the arms alternate open and crossed positions.
moves.focus: Choose one checkpoint at a time, preserving the arm crossing.

steps.title: Cross from open
steps.body: At the side position, travel through depth into the crossed-arm side position.

steps.title: Use the vertical exit
steps.body: Continue around until the top position, then pass through depth to the lower position.

steps.title: Complete the four exits
steps.body: Use the next crossed-arm side exit to reopen, then use the bottom exit to return upward.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

moves.name: Together-opposite isolation variation
moves.description: Repeat the crossing and vertical drill with isolations.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Allow the same open and crossed-arm positions as the antispin version.
moves.focus: Retain the six-point route while changing the driving style.

steps.title: Use the same checkpoints
steps.body: Locate open, crossed, top and bottom with together-opposite isolations.

steps.title: Carry through depth
steps.body: At each checkpoint, perform the corresponding isolation plane change, then continue the isolation path.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

moves.name: Split-opposite vertical shifts
moves.description: Use the audience-facing point while the hands occupy opposite vertical positions.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Begin facing the audience with space in front, behind and above; allow comfortable torso turns.
moves.focus: Keep track of which hand is high as the pair passes through depth.

steps.title: Establish top and bottom
steps.body: Start split-opposite antispins with one hand high and the other low.

steps.title: Pass toward the audience
steps.body: Carry the staves through the front-facing position, continue around and repeat with the other hand high.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

moves.name: Split-opposite side shifts
moves.description: At the side checkpoints, use the paired horizontal passage introduced in together same.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Begin facing the audience with space in front, behind and above; allow comfortable torso turns.
moves.focus: Find the side position before beginning the plane change.

steps.title: Reach the side checkpoint
steps.body: Bring the split-opposite pattern to the side, with the demonstrated thumb ends outward.

steps.title: Send the pinky ends forward
steps.body: Turn the pinky ends toward the audience, carry across to the other side and continue around.

steps.title: Repeat from the opposite side
steps.body: Perform the corresponding passage from the other side of the body.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

moves.name: Split-opposite alternating drill
moves.description: Combine right, top/bottom, left and opposite top/bottom exits.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Begin facing the audience with space in front, behind and above; allow comfortable torso turns.
moves.focus: Alternate side and vertical exits without losing the split timing.

steps.title: Shift from the right
steps.body: At the right-side checkpoint, carry the antispins across toward the left.

steps.title: Shift from high and low
steps.body: Continue until one hand is high, then use the front point again.

steps.title: Mirror the remaining exits
steps.body: Use the left-side exit, then the next high/low checkpoint, before repeating.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

moves.name: Split-same front and back shifts
moves.description: Use the back point for the first time: one staff travels toward the audience while the other travels away.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Allow the torso to turn; give the forward hand clearance above the shoulder.
moves.focus: The two staves occupy different depths instead of both coming forward.

steps.title: Find the staggered checkpoint
steps.body: In split-same antispins, reach the demonstrated position with one staff forward and the other back.

steps.title: Use front and back
steps.body: Send the two thumb ends outward toward the front and back points, then recover through the pinky-end positions into antispin.

steps.title: Check shoulder clearance
steps.body: Whichever hand is forward, place that staff's thumb end above the shoulder rather than below before making the passage.

steps.title: Repeat on both sides
steps.body: Continue antispins and repeat each time the corresponding front/back checkpoint returns.

diagramNotes: Must show simultaneous toward/away depth. The forward thumb end above the shoulder is a demonstrated constraint at 8:10-8:18. A front-view flat orbit is insufficient.

moves.name: Split-same top and bottom shifts
moves.description: Use the high/low checkpoint for a second split-same depth passage.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Begin facing the audience with space in front, behind and above; allow comfortable torso turns.
moves.focus: Keep one hand high and the other low as the pinky ends move outward.

steps.title: Reach top and bottom
steps.body: Continue the split-same antispin until the hands are at the vertical checkpoints.

steps.title: Pinky ends out and back
steps.body: Use the demonstrated pinky-end outward passage, then recover to the wall-plane antispins. Repeat from the opposite high/low arrangement.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

moves.name: Change timing during a plane shift
moves.description: Use shared depth positions to switch between split same and split opposites.
moves.grip: Center grip throughout; keep the thumb and pinky ends identifiable.
moves.stance: Begin facing the audience with space in front, behind and above; allow comfortable torso turns.
moves.focus: Choose whether the two ends go toward the audience together or separate front/back.

steps.title: Split same to split opposites
steps.body: At the high/low checkpoint in split same, send both ends toward the audience and then away to enter the split-opposite route.

steps.title: Split opposites to split same
steps.body: At a compatible point in split opposites, choose the split-same depth passage instead of sending both outward together.

steps.title: Apply the transition lesson
steps.body: Use the same shared-position logic as the previous lesson, now with the working plane changed.

diagramNotes: A depth-aware view is required: show audience-facing and away-from-audience points distinctly. A single flat trace does not reproduce this move.

pitfalls: Drawing only the four wall-plane points; toward and away are essential to the lesson.
Letting a plane change erase the identity of the thumb and pinky ends.
Sending both staffs forward during the split-same front/back variant.
Putting the forward thumb end below the shoulder in the split-same side passage.
Combining every exit immediately; drill one axis and one timing mode first.

evidence.observation: Drex lists right, top, left and bottom, then adds toward and away to describe an octahedron.
Direct frame shows the one-staff audience-facing passage.
Direct frame shows the together-same side checkpoint before the paired depth passage.
Drex explains visiting three diamond points before crossing to the opposite point.
Direct frame confirms crossed arms during the together-opposite side passage.
Direct frame confirms both staff ends aimed toward the camera in the together-opposite vertical example.
Drex explicitly identifies first use of the back point in split same.
The direct frame and narration establish the forward thumb end above shoulder level.
Both ends toward the audience are offered as a way to move from split same to split opposites.

limitations: These summaries follow the demonstrated starting facings; thumb-versus-pinky exit cues change if a learner reverses the initial prop facing.
The six-point map is a spatial teaching model, not measured motion capture or a demand for exact straight-line tip trajectories.

The explicit isolation demonstrations occur in together same and together opposites; Drex also says to practice the same ideas across timing/direction combinations, but does not separately break down every isolation variant.
A single fixed camera sometimes obscures which end is farther away. Depth-sensitive passages require the source view and a clearly labeled schematic, not claims of reconstructed 3D motion.

title: Crossers
summary: Turn shoulder and hip reels into crossers by keeping the arms crossed across the body. Learn together-same and split-opposite versions, then enter from a hybrid.

setup.grip: Use center grips. Together-same starts with thumb ends up; split-opposites starts with pinky ends pointing outward.
setup.stance: Cross the arms with each hand on the non-native side. Turn from one side-facing position to the other, adjusting the feet comfortably.
setup.plane: Reel passages move behind the shoulders and under the armpits while the body turns. Preserve the front/behind distinction.

moves.name: Together-same crosser
moves.description: Turn between side-facing positions with the arms crossed, alternating the high and low reel passages.
moves.grip: Both thumb ends start up. Either arm may be on top.
moves.stance: Cross the arms and turn slightly toward the left-side starting position.
moves.focus: Thumb ends rise at the side-facing checkpoints; pinky ends rise between them.

steps.title: Set the crossed arms
steps.body: Keep each hand across the body on the opposite side, with both thumb ends upright.

steps.title: Pass behind the shoulders
steps.body: As you turn from left-facing to right-facing, tuck the staves behind the shoulders. Return to both thumb ends up at the far-side checkpoint.

steps.title: Pass under the armpits
steps.body: As you turn back toward the left, use the lower passage underneath the armpits. Recover the thumb-up side position.

steps.title: Join the turns
steps.body: Repeat continuously. Check that the staves clear the body on each high and low passage rather than forcing the turn.

diagramNotes: Needs body rotation plus front/behind occlusion. A flat front-view circle cannot show the shoulder and underarm passages.

moves.name: Split-opposite crosser
moves.description: Keep the arms crossed while one pinky end rises and the other falls during each side-to-side turn.
moves.grip: Start with both pinky ends pointing outward from the body.
moves.stance: Arms crossed; begin in the left-side position shown in the tutorial.
moves.focus: Alternate which hand has its pinky end high during the turn.

steps.title: Turn toward the right
steps.body: Let the right pinky end rise and the left pinky end fall through the middle of the turn. Finish with both pinky ends pointing toward the right-side position.

steps.title: Return toward the left
steps.body: Let the right pinky end fall and the left pinky end rise through the middle. Finish with both pinky ends toward the left-side position.

steps.title: Keep the arms crossed
steps.body: Repeat right-pinky-up, then left-pinky-up, while the body turns side to side. Maintain space for each staff around the arms.

diagramNotes: Show crossed arms throughout and opposite vertical tip travel at the middle. One hand is farther from the camera in the initial side view.

moves.name: Hybrid entry to together-same crosser
moves.description: Enter the crossed-arm shape from an antispin/isolation hybrid.
moves.grip: Use the corrected pinky-end-in hybrid orientation shown after 3:48.
moves.stance: Begin open enough to perform the hybrid; turn as the rising staff passes behind the shoulder.
moves.focus: One staff goes behind the shoulder/head while the other remains in front.

steps.title: Check the facing
steps.body: Set the antispin/isolation hybrid with the pinky end inward. Drex corrects his first attempt before demonstrating this setup.

steps.title: Take the rising hand behind
steps.body: As the right hand comes up and over in the demonstrated version, route its staff behind the shoulder while keeping the other in front.

steps.title: Continue with crossed arms
steps.body: Let that front/behind relationship lead into the crossed-arm reel, then continue the together-same crosser.

diagramNotes: The exact entry includes depth and torso rotation; use the corrected source passage at 3:48-4:06. Do not animate the acknowledged wrong-facing attempt as instruction.

moves.name: Hybrid entry to split-opposite crosser
moves.description: Use the same front/behind entry principle to reach the split-opposite crosser.
moves.grip: Keep the center grip and check the pinky-end relationship for the split-opposite version.
moves.stance: Use the hybrid setup, then let the arms settle into the crossed position.
moves.focus: Separate one staff behind the head from the other in front.

steps.title: Prepare the split-opposite route
steps.body: Use the demonstrated hybrid/antispin approach with the facing needed for the split-opposite crosser.

steps.title: Create the depth separation
steps.body: Guide one staff behind the head while the other stays in front. This lets the arms cross without sending both staffs through the same space.

steps.title: Continue side to side
steps.body: Carry into the alternating right-pinky-up and left-pinky-up crosser established earlier.

diagramNotes: The source gives the front/behind principle and a brief demonstration, not a full endpoint-by-endpoint entry sequence.

pitfalls: Uncrossing the arms while turning; the crossed position defines the move.
Moving both staffs through the same side of the body during an entry.
Forcing the shoulder passage without checking body clearance.
Using the initial wrong-facing hybrid attempt at 3:33-3:46 instead of the corrected pinky-end-in version.
Confusing the performer's right and left with screen right and left.

evidence.observation: Drex defines crossers as hip/shoulder reels with the arms crossed.
Direct frame shows the crossed-arm thumb-up setup.
Direct frame shows the upper passage at shoulder/head height while turning.
Direct frame shows the lower passage beneath the arms.
Drex names the second version split-time opposites.
Direct frame shows opposite vertical tip orientations at the middle of the split-opposite turn.
Drex corrects the hybrid facing to pinky end inward.
Direct frame shows crossed arms reached from the corrected entry.
The closing explanation says one staff goes behind the head while the other stays in front.

limitations: The tutorial describes 180-degree turns between side-facing positions. The diagram should show those body turns, not two staff circles around a stationary front-facing figure.
The first together-same verbal description is less clear than the subsequent explanation; the later over-shoulder/underarm distinction and direct frames are used here.
Hybrid entries are briefly demonstrated. The split-opposite entry does not receive a complete separate thumb/pinky checkpoint breakdown.
Diagrams are teaching schematics rather than motion capture.
